name: Paris
type: metropolis; megacity; global city; territorial collectivity of France with special status; national capital; largest city
text: Paris is the capital and largest city of France, with an estimated city population of 2.04 million in an area of 105.4 km2 (40.7 sq mi), as of January 2026, and a metropolitan population of 13.3 million (2023). Located on the Seine in the centre of the Île-de-France region, it is the largest metropolitan area and fourth-most populous city in the European Union (EU). Paris is nicknamed the "City of Light" mainly due to its leading role in the Age of Enlightenment.

depictions.name: Paris
depictions.text: "This city has seen better days, but the ole girl hasn't lost her charm." — Sean Paris is the capital of France, and is the main location of the events of The Saboteur. The city is home to many major characters and features several famous landmarks and important installations. Under heavy Nazi occupation, Sean must work with Resistance members stationed at various hidden headquarters around the city to fight back against occupying forces.

During the French Revolution, the city was divided into seven districts: Le Louvre, Île de la Cité, Le Marais, La Bièvre, Les Invalides, Quartier Latin, and Ventre de Paris. History Formation Paris was founded during the 3rd century BCE when the Celtic tribe built a fortified settlement on the Île de la Cité.Assassin's Creed: Unity – Roman era In 52 BCE, the Romans, led by Julius Caesar, conquered the Parisii Celts who inhabited the area and built a town on the Seine river, named Lutetia Parisiorum ("Swamp of the Parisii").Assassin's Creed: Valhalla – The Siege of Paris The Petit Pont was built connecting the main island to the South bank of the river serving as the outlet to the roads leading to Orléans and Lugdunum.Assassin's Creed: Unity – Database: Petit Pont By the 1st Century CE, a group known as the Hidden Ones installed a bureau to operate in the city.Assassin's Creed: Valhalla – The Siege of Paris – Hidden In the late 3rd century, Paris and its surrounding region were converted to Christianity.
